title: podman build layer finalization slows in 5.8.7 vs 5.8.4 with fuse-overlayfs in Kubernetes
body:
### Issue Description

In a Kubernetes CI executor running rootful Podman inside a container, `podman build` using the official `quay.io/podman/stable` image became about 3 times slower between Podman 5.8.4 and 5.8.7. The slowdown is concentrated in the silent period after a `RUN` command finishes and before the next `STEP` appears. The measured build does not include a registry push or CI artifact creation/upload.

We compared the same immutable application source and Dockerfile on the same Kubernetes worker, using these pinned image digests:

- 5.8.4: `quay.io/podman/stable@sha256:3c99be9108dacd2b25d2f343c91386abd14a5ceaca68aa3e8d7f6ee2ebd50a16`
- 5.8.7: `quay.io/podman/stable@sha256:0da679a76d0ec35880419caeaf89b3627c3fbbc8e6cbf5456b69368b58bac628`

Both images use the overlay storage driver with `fuse-overlayfs` 1.17, ext4 backing storage, and `Native Overlay Diff: false`. This may involve Buildah or containers/storage layer finalization; the timing evidence alone does not establish which component is responsible.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

The generic probe below runs in two sequential Kubernetes CI pods, once per image digest above. Both pods use the same runner configuration. The 128 MB single-file layer alone finishes quickly on both versions. Adding 50,000 small files makes the difference visible.

```Dockerfile
FROM alpine:3.20
RUN dd if=/dev/zero of=/blob bs=1M count=128 && date -u '+payload_finished=%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
RUN mkdir /small-files && i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 50000 ]; do printf '%08d\n' "$i" > "/small-files/file-$i"; i=$((i + 1)); done; date -u '+small_files_finished=%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
RUN date -u '+next_step_started=%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
```

Run `podman build --no-cache -t localhost/podman-probe:latest .` with timestamped CI logs. No registry push is involved.

### Describe the results you received

| Measurement | 5.8.4 | 5.8.7 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full application `podman build` | 586 s | 1,782 s |
| `yarn install` command itself | 151 s | 203 s |
| Quiet period after `yarn install` until next `STEP` | 142 s | 764 s |
| `yarn build` command itself | 186 s | 193 s |
| Quiet period after `yarn build` until next `STEP` | 82 s | 569 s |
| Generic probe: 50,000-file `RUN` completion to next `STEP` | 21 s | 36 s |
| Generic probe: final `COMMIT` to `build_finished` | 14 s | 27 s |

The application image is approximately 1.69 GB. The actual application commands changed much less than the inter-step pauses. The generic probe showed the same direction but a smaller effect: total CI job time was 57 s versus 84 s. A single 128 MB file without the many-file layer took only about 12 s versus 14 s per CI job.

### Describe the results you expected

Layer finalization on 5.8.7 should be comparable to 5.8.4 for the same source and storage configuration, or the difference should be explained by an intended change.

### podman info output

Relevant sanitized fields from both runs:

```yaml
host:
  os: linux
  arch: amd64
  kernel: 6.8.0-1067-azure
store:
  graphDriverName: overlay
  graphOptions:
    overlay.mount_program: /usr/bin/fuse-overlayfs
    overlay.mountopt: nodev,fsync=0
  graphStatus:
    Backing Filesystem: extfs
    Native Overlay Diff: "false"
    Supports d_type: "true"
    Using metacopy: "false"
  backingMountFilesystem: ext4
fuse-overlayfs: "1.17"
```

### Podman in a container

Yes, in a Kubernetes CI pod.

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootful Podman in the CI container.

### Upstream Latest Release

No. The latest upstream release is 6.1.2. This report compares the supported 5.8 series supplied by the official `quay.io/podman/stable` image; `v6.1.2` is not available as a tag on that image. We tested the latest 5.8 image available to this pipeline.

### Additional environment details

Linux amd64 Kubernetes executor; the Podman container runs on a Linux worker with an ext4-backed writable container layer. The regression was observed with unchanged application build inputs and then checked with the generic Dockerfile above. The exact application repository and private CI logs are not public; sanitized timestamps and timings are included here.

comments.body:
There are significant pkg/archive changes to fix several archive security vulnerabilities.
The amount of bump here surprises me, it may be that we are doing "to much" extra work or maybe the syscall overhead is just that much. Do you see similar numbers without fuse-overlayfs, i.e. native kernel overlay?

cc @mtrmac @giuseppe
I do not have an easy way to test it with different settings
Can you install `strace` and run the podman build command with `strace -f -c podman build ...` and then paste the syscalls counts in both cases. I wonder if we do a lot more syscalls now.

I could reproduce this locally outside Kubernetes. I ran the two `quay.io/podman/stable` images as privileged Docker Desktop containers (WSL2 kernel 6.18) with `/var/lib/containers` on an ext4 volume. The smallest case that shows the slowdown needs no build at all: `podman commit` of a container that created many small files.

```bash
# inside a privileged quay.io/podman/stable container (default storage.conf: fuse-overlayfs)
podman run --name filler docker.io/library/alpine:3.20 sh -c \
  'mkdir /small-files && i=0; while [ $i -lt 50000 ]; do echo $i > /small-files/file-$i; i=$((i+1)); done'
time podman commit -q filler localhost/committed:latest
```

For native overlay I commented out `mount_program` and set `mountopt = "nodev"`, because the kernel overlay rejects `fsync=0`. That gives `Native Overlay Diff: true`.

Timings with 50,000 files, one run each, no strace:

| | 5.8.4 | 5.8.7 | ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| fuse-overlayfs: `podman commit` | 60.6 s | 96.4 s | 1.59x |
| fuse-overlayfs: `podman build` (probe without the 128 MB step) | 96.5 s | 161.1 s | 1.67x |
| native overlay: `podman commit` | 6.8 s | 9.1 s | 1.34x |
| native overlay: `podman build` | 11.9 s | 13.7 s | 1.15x |

Images: 5.8.4 `sha256:3c99be9108dacd2b25d2f343c91386abd14a5ceaca68aa3e8d7f6ee2ebd50a16`, 5.8.7 `sha256:f345d8d4fddea244d3a1ced27bcec82d14cc9e32cb5ead7f5882b0baf59dc8b0` (`v5.8.7-immutable`).

To see which process makes the extra calls, I traced only the `podman commit`, with 10,000 files, using `strace -f -Y` (the `-Y` flag labels each call with the process name):

| process | fuse 5.8.4 | fuse 5.8.7 | native 5.8.4 | native 5.8.7 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `podman` | 166,824 | 705,617 | 142,256 | 462,470 |
| `fuse-overlayfs` | 482,698 | 1,005,070 | – | – |
| `exe` (storage chroot) | 120,455 | 130,465 | 120,459 | 130,460 |

Only a subset of syscalls was traced: open/close, fcntl, epoll_ctl, xattr, stat, and read/writev/splice.

The extra calls come from the `podman` process while it generates the layer diff. `fuse-overlayfs` then has to serve each of them. For each file, 5.8.4 makes a few calls on the full absolute path: `newfstatat`, `lgetxattr`, `llistxattr` and a single `openat`. With fuse-overlayfs that path is under `merged/`; with native overlay it is under `diff/`. 5.8.7 resolves paths relative to directory file descriptors instead:

```
openat(9, "file-1234", O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_PATH) = 10   # x3, one per xattr call
openat(9, "file-1234", O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC) = 10
```

The parent directory is also reopened for almost every file. With 10,000 files in `/small-files`, 5.8.7 opens `small-files` 80,007 times with fuse-overlayfs and 50,006 times with native overlay. `file-N` is opened 60,000 and 40,000 times. The xattr reads moved from `lgetxattr`/`llistxattr` to `getxattr`/`listxattr`, which suggests they now go through a `/proc/self/fd/N` path.

My guess, not verified in the code: if every xattr or stat call on an entry re-walks the path from the root one component at a time, the cost grows with path depth as well as file count. That would explain why our real build is hit much harder than this flat probe. Its slow steps are `yarn install` and `yarn build`, which write deep `node_modules` trees; the pause after `yarn install` went from 142 s to 764 s.

I bisected this to podman-container-tools/container-libs@5f654a0359db4052c925139ad8628ff85aef5dea, "Make creating tars, Changes etc. safe against concurrent modification". It shipped in `go.podman.io/storage` v1.62.1, which Podman 5.8.7 vendors; 5.8.4 has v1.62.0. The same change is d5a0c9d42 on `main`.

Between the two storage releases, only the `archive.TarWithOptions` path changed noticeably. I checked that with a small Go program built against four storage source trees. It tars 50,000 five-byte files and discards the output. The files sit either directly under the root (depth 1) or eight directories deep (depth 8). Data was on ext4, run in `golang:1.25`, and each number is the best of 3 runs. No FUSE is involved:

| storage source | depth 1 | depth 8 | syscalls (depth 1, `strace -f -c`) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `storage/v1.62.0` | 1.15 s | 1.27 s | 876,381 |
| `2fc1207df` (parent of the commit) | 1.14 s | 1.29 s | 874,620 |
| `5f654a035` | 3.50 s | 9.10 s | 2,998,262 |
| `storage/v1.62.1` | 3.33 s | 8.85 s | 3,009,546 |

The per-file syscall counts at depth 1, before → after the commit: `openat` 1 → 9, `close` 1 → 9, `fcntl` 4 → 16, `epoll_ctl` 1 → 4 (all failing), and `newfstatat` 1 → 2. The `lgetxattr`/`llistxattr` calls become `getxattr`/`listxattr` on `/proc/self/fd/N`.

The cause seems to be that `RootLgetxattr` and `RootLlistxattr` each call `root.Open(path.Dir(fsPath))`. That walks the parent directory again from the root and wraps it in an `*os.File` (hence the `fcntl` and `epoll_ctl` calls). They then open the entry `O_PATH` for a single xattr call. `addTarFile` calls these per xattr and also does `root.Lstat` and `root.Open`, so every file entry resolves its parent path several times. The cost grows with depth: 50,000 files at depth 8 take 7x longer, versus 3x at depth 1.

With fuse-overlayfs and `Native Overlay Diff: false`, the diff is generated by walking `merged/`. Every one of those extra lookups becomes a FUSE request, which is why our CI builds, with deep `node_modules` trees, slowed so much more (the pause after `yarn install` went from 142 s to 764 s).

A possible fix, which I haven't tried: open the parent directory once per directory during the walk and reuse that fd for the stat, xattr and open calls on every entry in it, or at least once per entry. That would keep the concurrent-modification safety without re-walking the path for each call.

cc @mtrmac

thanks for the numbers, if confirmed this looks like a serious regression.  The effect is more visible with fuse-overlayfs because for IO syscall done by Podman will also cause more work for fuse-overlayfs

Some of the overhead is ~unavoidable to get the extra security but I didn’t anticipate that high a cost.

Ultimately the cause is that every single operation on an `os.Root` walks the entire path, in userspace. That should get better via https://github.com/golang/go/issues/73077 (with a pending PR), but probably only in a future Go version. Still, that sort of limits how much effort it is worthwhile to spend on a _temporary_ alternative.

---

> A possible fix, which I haven't tried: open the parent directory once per directory during the walk and reuse that fd for the stat, xattr and open calls on every entry in it

I agree that would be conceptually ideal; it’s not trivially possible given the `io/fs.WalkDir` implementation (and we can’t keep a handle for every parent directory open because that can run into handle limits with deeply nested structures). 

> or at least once per entry.

Yes, that should be easier to handle, although still not costless (when getting a file descriptor out of `os.Root` requires an extra `open()` syscall). And for the best possible performance we’d need to have a special Linux code path, ugh.

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/1216 is what we can easily do; more could be done, with more intrusive changes.

If you happened to already have a benchmarking set up / scripted, I’d appreciate running that against this version, to possibly reveal unanticipated surprises — full disclosure, I didn’t do _any_ measurements myself yet.

Thanks! I ran podman-container-tools/container-libs#1216 (head `9d6041549`) against its merge base on `main` (`cbc3ed865`) and both 1.62 releases. PR #1216 helps a lot for deep trees and does nothing for flat ones. `ChangesDirs` is untouched, and on fuse-overlayfs it is now the biggest remaining cost of the naive diff.

**Setup.** I built a static Go program once per storage source tree. It times `TarWithOptions`, `ChangesDirs(tree, empty)` and `ExportChanges(tree, changes)`, draining the tar streams to `io.Discard`. Each tree holds small files in a single directory, either one level deep (`level0/file-N`) or eight levels deep (`level0/.../level7/file-N`). It ran under Docker Desktop (WSL2 kernel 6.18.40):

- **ext4:** files on an ext4 volume.
- **fuse-overlayfs 1.17:** files in an overlay upper directory with an empty lower directory, read through the `merged` mount. That is the same path `NaiveDiffDriver` walks when `Native Overlay Diff: false`.

Every number is the best of 4 runs (2 interleaved rounds × 2 runs).

| filesystem | tree | operation | v1.62.0 | v1.62.1 | main base | PR #1216 | PR vs main |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ext4, 50,000 files | 1 level | tar | 1.17 s | 3.29 s | 3.23 s | 3.11 s | -4% |
| ext4, 50,000 files | 1 level | changes | 0.48 s | 1.72 s | 1.68 s | 1.76 s | +5% |
| ext4, 50,000 files | 1 level | export | 3.33 s | 6.06 s | 6.02 s | 5.96 s | -1% |
| ext4, 50,000 files | 8 levels | tar | 1.26 s | 8.81 s | 8.84 s | 4.19 s | -53% |
| ext4, 50,000 files | 8 levels | changes | 0.59 s | 5.21 s | 5.09 s | 5.00 s | -2% |
| ext4, 50,000 files | 8 levels | export | 3.55 s | 11.75 s | 11.59 s | 7.03 s | -39% |
| fuse-overlayfs, 20,000 files | 1 level | tar | 8.40 s | 16.34 s | 16.04 s | 15.70 s | -2% |
| fuse-overlayfs, 20,000 files | 1 level | changes | 3.30 s | 8.22 s | 7.99 s | 8.71 s | +9% |
| fuse-overlayfs, 20,000 files | 1 level | export | 8.05 s | 16.22 s | 16.09 s | 15.47 s | -4% |
| fuse-overlayfs, 20,000 files | 8 levels | tar | 8.31 s | 64.89 s | 67.63 s | 25.82 s | -62% |
| fuse-overlayfs, 20,000 files | 8 levels | changes | 3.30 s | 37.37 s | 41.11 s | 39.45 s | -4% |
| fuse-overlayfs, 20,000 files | 8 levels | export | 8.26 s | 65.15 s | 69.23 s | 25.44 s | -63% |

What I see:

- **Deep trees:** `tar` and `export` drop by 39–63%. The PR stops re-resolving the parent path for every operation on an entry. The remaining gap to v1.62.0 is still 2–3.3x (ext4 tar 4.19 s vs 1.26 s; fuse-overlayfs export 25.4 s vs 8.3 s).
- **Flat directories:** no measurable change. With one level, every entry still pays for `root.OpenRoot(parent)` plus the per-entry calls, and that costs about the same as before.
- **`ChangesDirs`:** unchanged by the PR and still 2.6–12x slower than v1.62.0. On fuse-overlayfs with 8 levels it takes 39 s versus 3.3 s. `NaiveDiffDriver.Diff` runs `ChangesDirs` and then `ExportChanges`, so a fuse-overlayfs commit of that tree costs about 11.6 s on v1.62.0, 110 s on the main base and 65 s with the PR. Once the PR is in, `ChangesDirs` accounts for about 60% of what remains.

Every run finished without errors (the harness aborts on any error), but I only measured timing, not output. I haven't benchmarked a Podman build with the PR vendored. I can do that if a test binary or image is available.

OK, another version of https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/1216 .
- Caches open directory handles much more
- Reimplements `ChangesDirs` to also keep individual-directory handles
- The xattr changes now cache the directory handle, as well as the individual handle.

Microbenchmarks in a non-representative environment suggest that this should be broadly comparable to the previous code. To do more, we would have to reimplement `fs.WalkDir` (and that might result in a small speedup), and I’d really prefer to avoid that complexity.
